why.rationale: The entry foyer (lines 47-160) is genuine shared furniture — arg-parse, mode-detect, RUN_DIR, log_event all live where every visitor can use them. But past the decision-desk the topology degrades: door-A is wrapped in a giant if-block (195-410) rather than extracted as a function, so it cannot be called from door-B and cannot share its room-packet construction logic. The two doors therefore reimplement the same flow with cosmetic differences (flat 2-digit vs cycle-ringed 3-component filenames; bare vs sidecar-state walks). The default-ticket at line 184 makes the older door silently authoritative — new visitors must speak the new word or they fall through. The doubled `exit 0` at 696-697 is the building's confession that door-B was nailed onto the back wall.
decisions_considered: wrapped-if vs extracted-function for door-A's flow
sidecar relay-state.json vs unifying both doors under one state model
flat NN.slug vs cN.NN.slug envelope naming (treating cycle=1 as the unifying case)
default 'parallel' ticket vs requiring explicit pattern declaration
substrate-first path resolution for pair-relay only (door-A has no equivalent)
